message:
Power-Systems Engineer:

Manager, the regulated feed has a low-wind gap that blocks the proposal in C26 locomotive-grid feed. Plain words: the regulator sleeps below its start volts so at light wind the tunnel load sees nothing. I read the Buck/Boost Converter - 8-40V to 12V/3A | Little Bird Electronics (E60) which needs 8 V minimum input, while low-wind volts (E37) are 6.50 V below that though top volts (E36) 14.3 V fit; I recompute because 220 Kv cannot span the window, and 170-180 Kv gives 8.41 V low and 18.5 V top (E76) inside 8-40 V, about a laptop charger holding steady instead of dropping out.

Safety-Control Integrator, I confirm what you take from the Braking ideas for wind turbines (E42) that almost all rotor brakes are spring-applied fail-safe. Plain words: the resistor helps slow the spin but goes limp when stopped so only the spring pad can keep it parked. From power side this means the 4 ohm dump in C26 locomotive-grid feed is a slowing aid not a park means, which is why the electrical-only runaway needs the 0.800 N-m spring hold.

Not ready, because blocking objection O2 to C26 locomotive-grid feed for 6.50 V below 8 V minimum stands until the Manager changes to 170-180 Kv.
